newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Wednesday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Wednesday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Wednesday:

In response to a question, spokesman Gerry Kiely defended the Commission's action in the fight against BSE. Kiely said the Commission changed its policy in 1994 after new scientific research on BSE and that this information had not been available before.

Spokesman Patrick Child said a sub-group of several member state central banks and Eurostat representatives met in Franfurt on Monday. The object was to analyse the procedure used by European Union's statistics office Eurostat director general Yves Franchet to reach a conclusion on recent France Telecom transfer of funds, he said. Child said whereas discussions would continue, the decision itself would not be modified.

Spokeswoman Barbara Nolan denied that a report on competitiveness submitted by DG III would be supressed. She also denied that the Commission had pulled out a chapter showing a link between higher unemployment and rigid labour market rules.
The Commission released the following documents:
- IP/96/981: Commission's Green Paper opens public debate on environmental noise reduction.
- Speech/96/269: Speech by Commissioner Edith Cresson at Cranfield University.
- Speech/96/270: Speech by Commissioner Edith Cresson at the 1996 Irish innovation lecture.
- Speech/96/271: Speech by Commission President Jacques Santer to the European aerospace industry.
- Speech/96/272: Speech by Commission President Jacques Santer on "Can Europe generate more jobs and more growth?"
- Eurostat; Statistics in focus - Agriculture, forestry and fisheries No 1996-11: Proceedings of Eurostat international seminar on "Income statistics for the agricultural household now available".
- Eurostat; Statistics in focus - Energy and industry No 1996-31: Signs of upturn in industrial activity.
